subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction/memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current serialized lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the durable fix changes scheduler and session-state ordering guarantees for interactive turns versus context maintenance.

options.title: Isolate maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

options.title: Preempt active maintenance
options.body: Keep the lane model but make maintenance abortable and reschedulable when user messages arrive, preserving stricter ordering at the cost of scheduler complexity.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Treat the current 180-second timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient, leaving foreground turns blocked during active compaction windows.

recommendation.title: Isolate maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior provenance connects this area to the central compaction/session-lane files, and the decision spans the scheduler contract rather than one related PR.
